column1: # VENDOR_ONLY.tsv -- addresses v1018-D024, precondition of v1018-D026.
# Files that live in vendor/ and have NO upstream counterpart.
# sync_vendor.sh replaces a vendored tree wholesale (`rm -rf "$abs_vendor"`,
# then untar the upstream export). That is correct behaviour for a mirror: a
# file absent upstream is, from the mirror's point of view, a file that should
# not be there. So a vendor-only file is deleted on every sync, silently.
# The divergence patch does not save it either: `--regen-patch` strips
# vendor-only new-file hunks, so the protection evaporates the moment anyone
# regenerates. Today's green is an accident of nobody having regenerated
# This turns "a file someone has to remember" into "a declared exception the
# tooling enforces". sync_vendor.sh restores every path listed here after the
# swap; tests/test_vendor_only_survives_sync.sh fails the build if one vanishes.
# Making Doctor vendoring automatic (v1018-D024) is unsafe until this exists,
# which is why it lands inside Part 2 rather than after it.
# ADDING A ROW IS A LAST RESORT. A vendor-only file cannot be reviewed upstream
# and drifts from the source it belongs to. Prefer landing the file in its home
# repo. If you must add one, say WHY there is no upstream, so the next person
# can retire it rather than inherit it.
#   owning_repo       repo the surrounding tree is vendored FROM
#   why_no_upstream   one line; the reason, not a description

column3: Cut-side cron entrypoint for the bundled Doctor. Written for the installer's launchd layout, which has no equivalent in HR015 where Doctor runs as a service. Deleted by the v1.0.18 re-vendor; recovered by hand. Retire by moving it to HR015 behind an is-native-deployment switch.
Test for the above. Same reason; must move with it.

Ostler Pro subscription gate (G0). Vendor-only: it exists in NO CM041 commit, and install.sh does `from subscription_gate import activate_first_month_free` to grant the 30-day free month. A re-pin of cm041/assistant_api on 2026-08-11 deleted it, which would have shipped an installer with a dangling import behind a clean-looking commit. Retire by upstreaming it into CM041 behind an is-bundled-deployment switch, the same shape as the doctor rows above.

Vendor-side import smoke test for the bundled assistant_api. Exists in no CM041 commit; the manifest note names it vendor-only, but nothing told the tooling, so the 2026-08-11 re-pin deleted it. Retire when the bundled-deployment import path is covered upstream.
Package marker for the vendor-only assistant_api test suite below. Excluded from the freshness diff, so a re-pin drops it and the three suites stop collecting.
Guards subscription_gate.py, itself vendor-only (row above). The gate was saved by its registry row on 2026-08-11 while the test that proves it works was deleted in the same run.
Guards the bundled subscription endpoint wiring. Same reason as the row above: it protects vendor-only code, so it can only live vendor-side.
Asserts the ical-server wire shape the installer depends on, against the VENDORED copy (431 lines diverged from source). Upstream cannot carry it because upstream is not the shipped file.

Repairs v1018-D658: elects one displayName per person and demotes the rest, for people already written before CM051 #548 fixed the writer. Vendor-only and never upstream -- it exists in NO HR015 commit (checked across --all, zero hits), because it repairs the SHIPPED graph on a customer box and HR015 has no such graph to repair. It is load-bearing, not dead: .github/workflows/name-repair.yml triggers on this exact path, and tests/test_name_repair.sh plus tests/helpers/check_name_repair.py and check_repair_guards.py all read it. The 2026-08-12 ostler_fda re-vendor would have deleted all 378 lines and taken the workflow's only subject with it. Retire by upstreaming into HR015 behind a repairs-a-deployed-graph switch, same shape as the doctor and subscription_gate rows above.

Vendor-side integrity test for the bundled browser-history ingest. Exists in NO HR015 commit (checked --all, zero hits). LOAD-BEARING IN CI: .github/workflows/vendor-integrity.yml names this exact file, so the 2026-08-12 re-vendor would have deleted the workflow's own subject and left a job that passes over nothing. Retire when the bundled ingest path is covered upstream.
Sibling of the browser-history row above, for the bundled iMessage ingest. No upstream commit ever. Registered with its siblings so a future sync cannot take one of the three and leave the others.

Sibling of the two rows above, for the bundled WhatsApp ingest. No upstream commit ever. WhatsApp is non-negotiable for v1, so losing its vendor-side ingest test to a silent sync deletion is the worst of the three to lose.

Guards the provisional-displayName contract that repair_placeholder_names.py (row above) repairs. No upstream commit ever, because it asserts against the VENDORED writer. Same pairing as subscription_gate.py and its test: the code was registered and the test that proves it works was not.

v1018-D021 fast first pass: writes the four artefacts with no model call so a thread is readable on the tick it arrives instead of after six serialised model calls. TEMPORARY ROW. It is landing upstream in the same change (CM048 branch fix/v1018-d021-seed-first-pass), but the manifest pins cm048_pipeline at f348270 and cm048's verify is "skip" because the source object store is sick, so a sync today would delete it and leave vendor/cm048_pipeline/src/cli.py importing a module that is gone. Retire this row when the pin moves past the CM048 merge.

Vendor-side byte-walking regression test for the bundled iMessage bridge. Exists in NO HR015 commit (checked --all with a positive control on a path that IS upstream, so the zero is a measured absence and not a broken probe). It cannot live upstream as written: half its assertions are anti-regression checks against CM051's OWN install.sh (that the 3.14c phase does NOT register the LaunchAgent, after the 2026-05-28 assistant self-talk loop), and HR015 has no install.sh to assert against. NOTHING PROTECTED IT: the manifest excludes this exact basename from the vendored file-set, so it gets no new-file hunk in imessage_bridge.patch either, and the next tree swap would delete it silently. Retire when the bundled-deployment install semantics are covered upstream.

Regression test for the 2026-05-28 first-run clamp: with state.json absent, bridge.poll_once must append NOTHING to inbox.jsonl and must save state at the current MAX(ROWID). Before the fix it initialised last_rowid=0 and replayed all of chat.db, which is what produced the assistant self-talk loop. Exists in NO HR015 commit (same --all sweep and control as the row above); upstream tests/ carries test_bridge.py and __init__.py only. Doubly unprotected: the manifest excludes tests/ from the vendored file-set, so it gets no new-file hunk, AND it is referenced by nothing in this repo, so a silent deletion would surface as neither a failing test nor a broken import. Registered with its sibling above so a future sync cannot take one and leave the other.
